interpretation: On one identical native result, the old code rejects normalization, while the corrected code reaches and retains the speech-support rejection. This proves the normalization fix without silently accepting an unsupported onset.
The normal base.en CPU replay passes: acquisition 21.585 s, one region, no gaps, authored-SRT tracking p95 0.214 s and six completed analyses without native rejection.
The experimental small.en Metal-preferred replay now eventually learns a second region, recovering in 15.333 s. Whole-scene p95 is still 30.130 s and no gap is learned. This is not scene acceptance.

The two complete small-model replays use different window phases after initial setup: the first request takes 14.254 s before versus 0.617 s in the later run. Their recovery difference cannot be attributed solely to the annotation fix. Only the same-result comparison isolates that change.
